content.json:
# Defender for AI — Threat & Security Insights

This workbook relies on **Azure Resource Graph** (`SecurityResources` — Microsoft Defender for Cloud alerts), not on Log Analytics. It works **with no additional configuration** (unlike Log Analytics' `SecurityAlert` table, which requires an explicit continuous export from Defender for Cloud).

Prerequisite: **Microsoft Defender for AI Services** enabled (Standard tier) on the subscription containing your Azure AI Foundry / Cognitive Services resources.

Alerts covered (`AI.Azure_*` and `AI.AIModelScan_*` prefixes): jailbreak attempts, credential theft in an AI response, prompt injection (ASCII smuggling), phishing URL shared by the model, access from suspicious IP/Tor, "wallet" attacks (cost abuse), abnormal tool invocation, LLM reconnaissance, malware in an uploaded model.

Reference: [Alerts for AI services (Microsoft Learn)](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/defender-for-cloud/alerts-ai-workloads)

content.query:
SecurityResources
| where type == "microsoft.security/alerts"
| where properties.alertType startswith "AI."
| summarize TotalAlerts = count(),
            HighSeverity = countif(tostring(properties.severity) == "High"),
            MediumSeverity = countif(tostring(properties.severity) == "Medium"),
            LowSeverity = countif(tostring(properties.severity) == "Low"),
            DistinctAlertTypes = dcount(tostring(properties.alertType))

SecurityResources
| where type == "microsoft.security/alerts"
| where properties.alertType startswith "AI."
| extend AlertType = tostring(properties.alertType),
         DisplayName = tostring(properties.alertDisplayName),
         Severity = tostring(properties.severity),
         StartTime = todatetime(properties.startTimeUtc),
         Status = tostring(properties.status),
         ResourceId = tostring(properties.resourceIdentifiers[0].azureResourceId)
| summarize Count = count(), LastSeen = max(StartTime) by AlertType, DisplayName, Severity
| order by Count desc

content.json:
## Alert details (most recent)
Includes the targeted resource and timestamp — useful for investigating a specific incident and correlating with the Token Consumption workbook (same time ranges).

content.query:
SecurityResources
| where type == "microsoft.security/alerts"
| where properties.alertType startswith "AI."
| extend AlertType = tostring(properties.alertType),
         DisplayName = tostring(properties.alertDisplayName),
         Severity = tostring(properties.severity),
         StartTime = todatetime(properties.startTimeUtc),
         Status = tostring(properties.status),
         Description = tostring(properties.description),
         ResourceId = tostring(properties.resourceIdentifiers[0].azureResourceId)
| project StartTime, DisplayName, Severity, Status, ResourceId, Description
| order by StartTime desc
| take 50

content.json:
## Defender for AI Services extensions status
Checks that the plan's 3 extensions are in the expected state (`AIPromptEvidence` must be **On** to capture prompts/responses associated with alerts; `AIModelScanner` and `AIPromptSharingWithPurview` are optional depending on your needs).

👉 This information is not exposed by Resource Graph — check via CLI:
```bash
az security pricing show -n AI --query "{tier:pricingTier, extensions:extensions}"
```

⚠️ **Known limitation**: Defender alerts only surface after a suspicious behavior is actually detected — a "light" prompt injection test may trigger no alert if the content isn't deemed malicious enough by the detection models. Absence of an alert does not mean absence of risk, only absence of detection so far.
